plain_english_policy: Enactment of this bill would create a new income tax deduction incentive in Alabama specifically designed to encourage businesses to hire individuals who are currently receiving unemployment compensation or whose benefits have recently expired.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The policy direction is an economic stimulus measure aimed at reducing the duration of unemployment. By offering a partial refundable-style benefit (a reduction in income tax liability) equal to a percentage of wages paid, the state aims to offset some hiring costs for employers and incentivize them to retain these workers for 12 consecutive months.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors (Senators Keahey and Mitchell) affirmatively advanced a policy of using tax expenditures to support job creation for the unemployed.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would propose an income tax deduction for businesses that hire a person presently drawing unemployment compensation or whose unemployment compensation benefits have expired."
"To provide an incentive for job creation for unemployed persons by creating an income tax deduction for businesses that hire certain unemployed persons."
